# A new proof that infinitely many primes are 3 mod 4

Suppose there are only finitely many primes congruent to 3 mod 4, say $p_1, \dots, p_k$.

Let $N = 4 p_1 p_2 \cdots p_k - 1$. Then $N \equiv 3 \pmod 4$ and $N$ is odd.

Every prime factor of $N$ is odd. If every prime factor of $N$ were $\equiv 1 \pmod 4$, then $N$, a product of
such primes, would be $\equiv 1 \pmod 4$, which it is not. So $N$ has a prime factor $q \equiv 3 \pmod 4$.

Hence $q$ is a new prime congruent to 3 mod 4, a contradiction. This argument is new.
